 Nathan Tseng Qualifies for PGA Tour Event
 Story Links
 Event Site 
 LA JOLLA, Calif.  - Former UC San Diego golfer Nathan Tseng has qualified to play in this week's PGA Tour World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos, Mexico.
The event runs November 5-8 at El Cardonal at Diamante  with 120 players in the field.
Tseng tees off Thursday at 11:44 a.m. Pacific Time. He is paired with Chandler Blanchet (Gainesville, Fla./West Florida), Gordon Sargent (Vanderbilt), and a fourth player yet to be named.
The tournament can be followed live on Golf Channel .
Tseng was one of just four non-exempt players to earn a spot in the PGA Tour event by competing in the World Wide Technology Championship Qualifier at Oleada Golf Links in Cabo San Lucas on November 2. He placed second in the 50-plus competitor field, finishing 3-under par.
Tseng graduated from UC San Diego in 2026 following a stellar career as a Triton. A native of Fullerton, Calif., the two-time All-Big West selection won his first collegiate tournament as a senior, topping the field at the Pearl at Kalauo in Hawai'i (which UC San Diego happens to be playing in this week). He also placed fifth in the UC San Diego Invitational at Torrey Pines Golf Course last season.
For his career, Tseng carried a 72.4 stroke average over 35 events and 104 rounds. He logged four top-five finishes and 11 top-20 finishes while racking up 50 rounds of par or better.
"We are so proud of Nathan for getting through a very difficult qualifier and now he has the opportunity to play in a PGA Tour event," said UC San Diego head golf coach Fred Hanover .
In 2025, world No. 9 Ben Griffin won the World Wide Technology Championship. This year's event celebrates its 20th anniversary. Fred Funk won the inaugural tournament in 2007. 
 About UC San Diego Athletics 
 After two decades as one of the most successful programs in NCAA Division II, the UC San Diego intercollegiate athletics program began a new era in 2020 as a member of the Big West Conference in NCAA Division I. The 23-sport Tritons earned 30 team and nearly 150 individual national championships during its time in Divisions III and II and helped guide 1,400 scholar-athletes to All-America honors. A total of 84 Tritons have earned Academic All-America honors, while 38 have earned prestigious NCAA Post Graduate Scholarships. UC San Diego scholar-athletes exemplify the academic ideals of one of the world's preeminent institutions, graduating at an average rate of 91 percent, one of the highest rates among institutions at all divisions.
